briefings.title: AI Could Push Inflation Either Way, Says BOE’s Bailey

people.name: Kevin Warsh
people.role: Former Member, Federal Reserve Board of Governors

briefings.tldr: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey stated that AI could be either inflationary or disinflationary depending on whether demand shocks arrive before supply-side productivity gains.

briefings.title: LIVE: Andrew Bailey speaks at Reykjavik 2026 economic conference
briefings.tldr: At the Reykjavik economic conference, central bankers from the UK and US emphasized that persistent inflation—exacerbated by Middle East energy shocks and structural shifts like AI and aging demographics—requires highly flexible, state-contingent monetary frameworks and prolonged "higher-for-longer" interest rate environments.

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: BOE Governor Andrew Bailey to speak after rate decision
briefings.tldr: The Bank of England held its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75% in an 8-1 vote, taking previous expectations of rate cuts off the table due to Middle East conflict-driven energy price volatility.
